card.name: The word still before a verb
card.fires_on: The word "still" placed right after a subject or auxiliary (will, there, it'll) and before the main verb, meaning "even so" or "continuing to".

modes.label: Still after a will or there
modes.description: "still" follows will, there, or it'll and leads into a clause about what remains true or needed.
modes.example: The tablet(s) will not completely dissolve; there will<< still>> be small tablet clumps in the mixture

modes.label: Still after a noun subject
modes.description: "still" comes straight after a noun subject and before a past or present verb, meaning continuing.
modes.example: At that time, a few skilled groups of villagers<< still>> hunted and corralled the wild elephants

card.writes: It promotes words like remains and remain, which fit the idea of something continuing.
card.plain: It marks the word "still" when it means something continues or remains true despite a change.
